LOCAL PRICE & YIELD SENSITIVITY

Room for market uncertainty

Local evidence matters. Prices differ by country, market, crop grade, buyer, contract, season and date. AgriPulse never invents a local price: use a current farm-gate, cooperative, contract or wholesale quote.

FAOSTAT producer prices ↗World Bank benchmarks ↗

What these values mean

Weather and near-surface moisture are model values at a reference grid. A polygon describes your chosen boundary; its area does not make the weather data more precise. Rotation paths use general crop characteristics. Profit uses the assumptions you enter.

ABOUT AGRIPULSE

Built by students. Grounded in purpose.

Meet the school and team behind AgriPulse.

OUR SCHOOL

Dunia Alajial International School

AgriPulse was developed at Dunia Alajial International School, where students turn scientific ideas, technology and teamwork into projects designed to help people and communities.

Learn more ↗
OUR TEAM

The Tech Team

The Tech Team created the AgriPulse experience—from the visual identity and interface to the field planning tools that connect Earth observations with practical farm decisions.

01

Weather & water

Open-Meteo supplies modeled forecasts for your selected location. Rain and reference water demand help you compare the week ahead.

Explore Open-Meteo ↗
02

Earth observations

NASA POWER offers historical climate context for the region around your field. Its data describes a broader grid, not a soil test.

Explore NASA POWER ↗
03

Your local knowledge

Soil samples, crop choices, costs, and selling prices come from you. Update your inputs to make each scenario more relevant.

Choose your field →
04

NASA signals in context

AgriPulse is designed to grow toward SMAP soil moisture, ECOSTRESS heat, GPM rainfall, Landsat and MODIS vegetation, GRACE water storage, and SRTM elevation layers.

Browse NASA Earthdata ↗

NASA Space Apps challenge principle: AgriPulse compares the existing rotation with alternative strategies, explains the evidence and trade-offs, shows uncertainty, and supports—not replaces—farmer judgment and local agricultural expertise.
